newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer, Aramco talks set in S'pore.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer, Aramco talks set in S'pore.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices moved higher in afternoon trade on Friday, buoyed by overnight crude gains, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half July was quoted at $210.00/212.00 per tonne. On Thursday, it was sold by a Japanese trading house to a European trader at $209.00.
Levels for the second-half June contract remained about $1.00 lower than first-half July.
Term naphtha negotiations were set in the third week of May in Singapore for Saudi Aramco cargoes to be lifted in the July-December period, traders said.
In the first-round of bidding, at least one firm bid at about $15.00 per tonne over the Aramco formula for A-180, compared to a $6.50 premium set in last October, they said.

In low-sulphur waxy residue (LSWR), Indonesia announced its initial allocation for May lifting. However, traders came up with different estimates of the total volume, with Singapore traders assessing May allocation to total about 3.6 million barrels and Japanese traders 3.75 to 3.9 million.
A South Korean refiner sold 170,000 barrels of Malaysian LSWR cargo to be lifted in late May to a Japanese trading house, traders said. The price was not available.
